text:
nicole: FYI — Support escalated: customer cust-431 reporting p99 latency regressions on /v1/generate in us-west — p99 jumped from ~180ms to ~2.4s around 22:10 UTC. sample req: req_0a1b2c3. They see many timeouts.
sara: thx. do we have correlation_id / trace id from their request? any host/instance ids?
nicole: they included trace id trace-9f7 and a couple of logs, attaching snippet: `503 gateway timeout` then `rpc: deadline exceeded`
mike: seeing a small spike in us-west tail from our infra dashboards starting 22:08. p95 up ~1.1s, p99 ~2.3s. CPU on some nodes spiked, KV cache eviction increased.
kevin: rolled out a runtime kernel tweak to sequence batching heuristics at 21:55 in us-west canary. I'll check if rollout reached the affected pool.
sara: mitigation plan: 1) enable circuit-breaker for cust-431 at 10rps fallback 2) route their traffic to fallback model (redwood-compact) 3) enable regional fallback to us-east if us-west remains degraded. Who can flip these?
mike: I can apply a temporary policy. running: `redwoodctl policies create --type circuit_breaker --customer cust-431 --p99-ms 1000 --action fallback`
mike: applied circuit-breaker policy -> STATUS: active for cust-431. starting to see reduced error surface in logs.
kevin: I'm pausing the heuristic rollout in us-west and rolling the canary back to previous binaries on the affected pool. command: `deploy-bot rollback --service runtime --region us-west --tag v2024-11-06`
deploy-bot: rollback triggered for runtime in us-west to v2024-11-05-rc3. ETA ~4m.
sara: add short-term rate-limit guardrails so any single API key can't spike queueing: `req_per_min: 1200` and `concurrency: 8` for hosted-tier. That should keep latencies from cascading.
mike: done — lightweight rate cap set for hosted-tier in us-west. Monitoring shows queue lengths dropping.
kevin: kernel rollback finished, restarted affected nodes, KV eviction normalized. early signs p95 down to ~220ms, p99 ~480ms for most tenants.
nicole: told customer we enabled fallback to redwood-compact and a circuit-breaker, next steps if they still see issues: provide full HAR + trace, we can route entire org to us-east.
sara: follow-up playbook notes for postmortem: - root cause suspicion: batching heuristic + sequence-length distribution mismatch -> kernel path regression - short-term mitigations: circuit-breaker, fallback model, regional routing, rate cap - long-term: add canary traffic skew to catch p99 regressions, add automatic rollback on p99 delta > 30%
mike: logging note: create an alert that triggers when p99 increases 50% vs baseline AND KV cache evictions > 100/min in the same 5m window.
kevin: filing a revert PR and a small test harness to emulate long-tail sequences so we don't regress again.
sara: thanks team. nicole, please update the ticket and close after customer confirms improved latency or we route them to us-east.
nicole: will do — customer reported improvement after fallbacks. marking interim mitigation until engineering completes revert and expanded tests. :thumbsup:
